newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to host Moslem nations' ministerial meeting.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to host Moslem nations' ministerial meeting.

text.p: High-level officials from eight Moslem countries will meet in Turkey this weekend to discuss economic cooperation, a Turkish foreign ministry official said on Thursday.

Officials from Turkey, Egypt, Iran, Pakistan, Nigeria, Bangladesh, Malaysia and Indonisia will also discuss a possible summit between their leaders during the one-day meeting in Istanbul on Saturday, the Turkish official told Reuters.
The foreign ministers of Iran and Pakistan will also hold a trilateral meeting with Turkish officials on Sunday to discuss the situation in Afghanistan, he said.
Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan will make an opening speech at both meetings. He has visited all the participating countries, except Bangladesh, since coming to power in June.
Erbakan's attempts to draw NATO-member Turkey closer to the Moslem world have caused concern among Ankara's western allies.
The foreign ministry official said Saturday's talks could prepare the way for a summit of the eight countries' leaders in the first quarter of 1997.
An international conference aimed at halting the fighting in Afghanistan was held in Tehran in October. Pakistan, a key player in the region, stayed away from that meeting.

The hardline Islamist group Taleban took over the Afghan capital Kabul in September. Forces loyal to the ousted government and their ally General Abdul Rashid Dostum are now trying to win the city back.
"The goal of the (trilateral) meeting is to help find a solution for the situation in Afghanistan," the official said.
